headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear a greater share of grid infrastructure costs, aiming to reduce the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Dominion Energy
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: A Virginia bill seeks to shift more energy costs onto data centers, potentially saving residential customers over $65 annually. This legislation would require data centers to pay for their own electrical substations and capacity costs, with Dominion Energy supporting the measure.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This bill mandates that water suppliers report the total volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency for water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Virginia League of Conservation Voters
news_headline: New regulations beef up data centers' required water use reporting in Virginia
news_summary: New regulations, effective January 2027, will require waterworks operators to categorize monthly sales data, including water usage by data centers, to increase transparency. This bill aims to provide better data for water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulation
short_summary: This bill establishes requirements for site assessments regarding noise impacts on nearby residences and schools for new high-energy-use facilities, including data centers.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental advocates, Virginia League of Conservation Voters
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry
news_headline: Virginia hits data centers with a new energy tax and finally cracks down on water and noise
news_summary: Virginia has approved new regulations for data centers, including tighter rules on noise and water use, and a new energy consumption tax. HB 153 specifically addresses siting concerns by requiring noise assessments for high-energy-use facilities near residential areas and schools.
